overview: The Medford City Council and Community Development Board held a joint meeting to present and discuss proposed zoning amendments for the Boston Avenue corridor. After receiving substantial public feedback and reviewing proposed revisions, both bodies voted to continue the hearing to June 11, 2026.

items.title: Presentation on Current Conditions and Proposed Zoning Districts
items.summary: Emily Innes and Paula Ramos Martinez presented the existing zoning, land use, and proposed boundaries of the Boston Avenue corridor sub-districts.

items.title: Presentation on Zoning Text and Use Tables
items.summary: Emily Innes outlined the proposed text amendments, use differentiations, dimensional standards, and initial community feedback.

items.title: Discussion of District Boundaries and Proposed Standards
items.summary: Alicia Hunt and Emily Innes detailed the landmarks and proposed heights for sub-districts BA1, BA2, and BA3.

items.title: Council and Board Discussion of Proposed Zoning Rules
items.summary: City Councilors discussed local hiring regulations, parking mandates for lodgers, and use standards for drive-through pharmacies.

items.title: Presentation of Alternative Boundary and Height Proposals
items.summary: Chair Doug Carr presented alternative proposals recommending reduced heights for BA2 and BA3, the inclusion of St. Clement's properties, and the removal of Walkling Court.

items.title: Board Discussion on Specific Use Regulations
items.summary: Dina Caloggero recommended special permit requirements for doggy daycares and neighborhood medical offices, and discussed private student housing options.

items.title: Board Feedback on Density and Historic Preservation
items.summary: Ari Fishman supported higher building heights, increased density, and removing Walkling Court and lodging parking requirements.

items.title: Discussion on Topography, Parking Incentives, and Data Centers
items.summary: Page Buldini inquired about covered parking feasibility, setbacks around geological ledge, and potential data center zoning.

items.title: Board Feedback on Student Housing and Corridor Regulations
items.summary: Sean Beagan recommended allowing privately owned student housing with minimum bed sizes and excluding low-density residential structures from BA1.

items.title: Discussion on Board Purview and Transit Definitions
items.summary: John Anderson raised concerns about the Community Development Board's authority during site plan reviews, transit definitions, and gentrification.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents commented on proposed building heights, traffic congestion, rat control, student housing, and sidewalk widths.

items.title: Direction to Staff and Continuation of Hearing
items.summary: The City Council and Community Development Board compiled a list of suggested amendments and voted to continue the public hearing to June 11, 2026.

subject: Boston Avenue Corridor Zoning Amendments Public Hearing
